newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't sees re-election vote next week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't sees re-election vote next week.

text.p: The Brazilian government is aiming to hold on January 28 a first lower house vote on a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for a second term, a government whip said.

"Technically we could vote any time, tomorrow even, but we expect it will take place on Tuesday afternoon or evening," said Dep. Jose Anibal, lower house leader of Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democratic Party (PSDB).
The government had said it aimed to put the constitutional amendment allowing re-election to the first of two votes on the floor of the lower house January 22.
But opposition to the timing of the vote within the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), the largest in Congress, made that timetable impossible to meet.

Anibal said the government would submit the re-election amendment for inclusion in the voting schedule of the Chamber of Deputies on Thursday, blocking any other votes in the lower house until its approval.
